Connect with your ESPN League ID. Find it in your league's web URL, …/league?leagueId=XXXXXX — or just paste the whole URL and we'll pull the ID out.

Where do I find my League ID?
  • 1Open your league on fantasy.espn.com (desktop, or a phone browser — not the app).
  • 2Copy the whole address-bar URL — it contains leagueId=XXXXXX.
  • 3Paste the URL (or just the number) above — we'll find the ID.
private league?

Private leagues need two read-only codes from your ESPN cookies — they let us read your league, never change it. Grab them fast with the free ESPN Cookie Finder extension, or by hand (steps below).

SWID *
espn_s2 *
Where do I find these?
  • 1Open fantasy.espn.com and make sure you're logged in.
  • 2Open developer tools → Application → Cookies.
  • 3Copy the values of SWID and espn_s2 and paste them above.

SORT
Grade keys Upsideceiling / boom weeks Upside · ceilingBlends last season's boom-game rate (weeks hitting the position's boom line — QB 24, RB/WR 20, TE 15 pts), the player's weekly ceiling (85th-percentile game, ranked within position), and per-game scoring. Ascending youth (≤2 seasons) and a rising market add a small bump; rookies with no data are estimated from draft capital. Dynasty boards credit youth more (multi-year runway) and trim ceiling for age.0–10 · higher = bigger ceiling Floorweekly safety Floor · weekly safetyRewards a low bust-game rate (weeks under the position's bust line), a strong weekly floor (20th-percentile game vs position), and availability (games played ÷ 17). Proven, high-volume players score highest.0–10 · higher = safer week to week Riskinjury · volatility (lower = safer) Risk · downsideAdds risk for games missed across the last 3 seasons (durability — recent seasons count more, and a season missed entirely counts in full), week-to-week volatility (bust rate), age cliffs (RB ≥27 · WR ≥30 · TE ≥31 · QB ≥36), and a sharply falling ADP. Dynasty boards apply age earlier and more steeply — asset value fades before the production cliff. Shown 0–10 where lower is safer — the overall grade uses (11 − Risk).0–10 · lower = safer Situationalfit to your roster Situational · fit to youCombines your roster need (open starter slots, blended with positional scarcity), league scoring (PPR lifts pass-catchers), and the player's team-offense strength (weighed less on dynasty boards). Recalculates every pick as your roster fills — so the same player scores differently for different teams.0–10 · higher = better fit right now how the grade adds up ⓘ Player grade & team gradeA player's overall grade = mean(Upside, Floor, 11−Risk, Situational) on a 0–10 scale. Your Draft Grade averages that across your best starting lineup (QB / 2RB / 2WR / TE / 2FLEX by grade, bench excluded) and maps it to 0–100 + a letter. All factors are built from nflverse data (last-season PPG · boom% · bust% · weekly floor/ceiling, plus 3-season durability) and your league's scoring and roster settings.skill positions only · K/DST not scored
